result.summary: Both original BLOCKERs are genuinely closed. Independently re-derived, not copied from the rework's self-report or from the pre-existing step-01b-code-design-validator-recheck1.json already committed at 5ec70218 (that file made the same claim; treated as an unverified record per core-directives.md's handoff-factual-premises rule, not as evidence). BLOCKER 1 (AC4 grep): ran `grep -n -B1 -iE "title:.*\bentit(y|ies)\b" docs/requirements.yaml` myself against the live file -- exactly 1 match: `11714-  - id: REQ-207` / `11715:    title: Run Vortex's 4 simulation scenarios against Letflow (production-order budget gate, supplier-deviation critical/false-positive compensation, entity list filter/page) and report per-scenario findings`. Also ran `grep -c -iE "title:.*\bentit(y|ies)\b" docs/requirements.yaml` -> 1, confirming no double-count. The command is well-formed and re-runnable verbatim by a future reader (word-bounded \bentit(y|ies)\b, no longer the bare-substring \"entit\" pattern that false-positived on 'identity'). Section 4.1 (lines 578-606) states the corrected command, its exact expected output (the 11714/11715 block), and correctly identifies the match as REQ-207's own self-referential title via the -B1 id: line -- not a claim by another requirement. Section 4.3's evidence bullet (line 650) quotes the same corrected command and the same '1 match, id: REQ-207' result -- no stale reference to the old grep -c/claimed-0 wording remains anywhere (grepped the whole doc for 'grep -c' and for the literal string '[Ee]ntit' -- zero matches outside the one explanatory aside at line 581-584 that exists specifically to document why the old pattern is wrong, not to specify it as the check). BLOCKER 2 (OQ-1): grepped the whole doc for 'OQ-1' -- 3 locations, all checked: (a) line 57, §0.1 -- historical/forward-referencing prose ('this design is authored *as if* REQ-206 has already merged... Open question OQ-1 (§7) states the fallback plan explicitly if REQ-206 has *still* not merged') -- this is explaining the design's original reasoning and correctly points to §7, not itself asserting OQ-1 is currently open; (b) line 476, §3.2 -- 'see §5's open question OQ-1' -- this is a genuine section-number error (OQ-1 actually lives in §7, not §5; §5 is 'Test module structure', confirmed via `grep -n '^## §'` listing all 9 section headers) but it is PRE-EXISTING: diffed against the original FAILed version (`git show 4da89496:lib/letflow/design/req207-vortex-scenario-execution.md`) and the identical line/wording was already present before rework1 touched anything, so it is not a regression introduced by this rework and does not misstate OQ-1's resolution status (it misnumbers the section, it does not claim OQ-1 is open) -- filed as a MINOR issue below rather than a BLOCKER, consistent with 'never resolve a conflict silently' but not grounds to fail rework that fixed the actual two named defects; (c) line 761, §7 -- 'OQ-1 -- RESOLVED/MOOT (rework 1, this session)' with the full resolution: REQ-206 merge commit 2d068c79 named, both dependency facts re-confirmed, explicit statement that §0.1's fallback plan 'is therefore not exercised and does not apply'. All 3 locations checked; none reads as a live, unresolved open question. Independently re-ran `git log main --oneline | grep -i REQ-206` -- shows `2d068c79 REQ-206: SwiftRoute scenario execution (S7 simulation harness) (#767)`. Independently ran `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2d068c79 HEAD` -- exit 0 (is ancestor of this branch's HEAD). Independently read test/support/simulation/scenario_fixture.ex lines 40-41 directly: `@spec load!(path :: String.t()) :: Scenario.t()` / `def load!(path) do` -- confirmed present exactly as cited. Independently read test/support/simulation/runner.ex (this file, despite its path name, defines `Letflow.Simulation.Scenario`) lines 44-52: `@type step :: %{required(:via) => :api | :gui | :skip, ...}` -- line 45 confirmed, the :skip vocabulary extension is real and matches the citation. SANITY RE-CHECKS (lighter, since these already passed the first gate): grepped the 819-line doc for `defmodule`/`defstruct` and for `^\s*def ` -- zero matches, no implementation code introduced or remaining (22 code-fence delimiters / 11 fences, consistent with the prior pass's count after accounting for the rework's added fences). Grepped lib/letflow, test/support, test/letflow for `audit_event_ordering` outside the design doc -- zero matches, still genuinely new/unshipped. Read the live docs/requirements.yaml REQ-207 entry directly (lines 11713-11774): all 6 real acceptance_criteria strings match section 8's AC1-AC6 mapping table 1:1, no TBD, no criterion unmapped. Dependency claims (ScenarioFixture.load!/1, Runner's via vocabulary) independently confirmed above under BLOCKER 2. No new gaps found; the design is APPROVED.

Confirmed via `git show 4da89496:...` that this exact line was already wrong before rework1 (not a regression from this rework, and not one of the two BLOCKERs this recheck was scoped to). It does not misstate OQ-1's resolution status -- a reader following it to the (wrong) section number would simply need to look at §7 instead, where OQ-1 is correctly marked RESOLVED/MOOT. Not blocking this gate; recorded so it gets fixed at the source rather than silently carried forward again.
